facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage fell on earnings growth, not repayment. Total debt was USD 2,497.8 million at 2024-12-31, USD 2,490.8 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 2,599.1 million at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,186.6 million in FY2024 to USD 1,404.1 million in FY2025 and USD 1,552.6 million over the last twelve months. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore moved from 2.11x to 1.77x to 1.67x, and net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.03x to 1.72x to 1.62x. Debt rose by USD 108.3 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, the period in which the company replaced its revolving facility, used new 2034 notes to redeem half of the 2028 notes and sold a further USD 100.0 million of the 2034 notes in August 2026 to repay part of the revolver. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The issuer's own earnings measure is the more conservative guide to cash that reaches the parent. The issuer states only an Adjusted EBITDA, which deducts the income of noncontrolling interests, USD 160.9 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and adds back share-based compensation. Reported EBITDA, calculated here from pre-tax income, interest and depreciation, is USD 134.9 million higher than the issuer's measure for that period. On the issuer's measure total debt is 2.26x, 1.96x and 1.88x Adjusted EBITDA at the three dates, in line with the issuer's own rounded 2.0x at 2025-12-31 and 1.9x at 2026-09-30. Joint-venture partners received USD 141.8 million of distributions in the nine months, so the deduction is a cash cost and not an accounting convention. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 24, 47, 48; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C16; calculation C27

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation is strong but is largely absorbed by growth spending and distributions. In FY2025 net cash from operating activities of USD 1,175.6 million funded USD 736.4 million of capital spending and USD 152.1 million of joint-venture distributions, leaving USD 287.1 million; dividends and repurchases took USD 229.1 million of that and left USD 58.0 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 the same sequence left USD 198.7 million before dividends of USD 57.9 million and repurchases of USD 203.7 million, a shortfall of USD 62.9 million in a period when total debt rose by USD 108.3 million. Growth capital spending was USD 451.2 million in those nine months and capital spending ran at 12.88% of net operating revenues, so the pace at which leverage keeps falling is mainly a management choice. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is ample and refinancing risk is remote before 2028. At 2026-09-30 cash of USD 76.2 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 871.4 million, after USD 75.0 million drawn and USD 53.6 million of letters of credit, gave liquidity of USD 947.6 million, or 0.36x total debt. The revolver matures on 2031-03-09, so no facility expires within twelve months, and scheduled principal through 2027 is only USD 56.2 million. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a benign reading is that growth and returns are being financed at the margin by debt. Capital spending of USD 617.2 million in nine months compares with a 2026 plan of USD 920 million to USD 995 million and about USD 535 million still to spend on projects under construction, and the board raised the repurchase authorization in July 2026. Receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in the nine months against USD 18.8 million a year earlier, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, which the issuer attributes to a billing and collecting disruption after a system conversion. If operating cash flow does not cover the remaining planned spending, or repurchases continue above free cash flow, leverage on the issuer's measure would stop falling. The view would improve if debt were repaid from free cash flow while EBITDA keeps growing, and weaken if trailing EBITDA fell, if the revolver were drawn to fund distributions, or if the covenant ratios, once supplied, showed less headroom than the compliance statements imply. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 35, 43, 44; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C42

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and 92% of patients are referred from acute-care hospitals, so a payment-rule or referral shock would reach revenue directly. facts.text: Payment policy, not demand, is the main business risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, with Medicare alone at 65.7% for the nine months and 66.3% in the third quarter. Rates are reset each year by the federal payer, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 adds a net 2.3% to Medicare payment rates from October 2026, which supports pricing. The same payer is widening claim review: a demonstration that puts claims through pre-claim or post-payment review reached Texas in March 2026 and California in May 2026, and from January 2027 will cover about 63% of the company's Medicare claims. Denied claims of USD 39.0 million were under review at 2025-12-31, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, so slower or lower collection is where a payment-policy shock would first reach cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124, 161; calculation C1

About 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures with health systems that also refer patients. The company lists partner operating or financial strain as a risk, so a partner problem would be both a volume risk and a possible cash call. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth is capital-hungry, so cash flow is committed to expansion before it is available for debt reduction. The network added 16 hospitals between the end of 2023 and 2026-09-30, and new capacity contributed 2.9 percentage points of the 5.2% discharge growth in the nine months, which is more than half of it. The 2026 capital plan is USD 920 million to USD 995 million, of which USD 225 million to USD 240 million is maintenance, with about USD 535 million more to finish projects now under construction. The non-maintenance part is discretionary, which gives management a lever in a downturn, but it also means leverage falls only if growth spending slows or earnings keep outrunning it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 36, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11; calculation C9; calculation C7; calculation C17

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder returns are the creditor-relevant behaviour to watch, and they are rising while evidence of the legal room for them is not supplied. The quarterly dividend rose from USD 0.17 to USD 0.19 per share in July 2025 and to USD 0.21 in July 2026, repurchases rose from USD 31.1 million in FY2024 to USD 158.0 million in FY2025 and USD 203.7 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the board raised the repurchase authorization to USD 1.0 billion in July 2026. Dividends and repurchases took 19.49% of operating cash flow in FY2025 and 27.32% in the nine months, and in the nine months they exceeded the USD 198.7 million left after capital spending and joint-venture distributions by USD 62.9 million. The March 2026 credit agreement also relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, which widens the room for such returns, while no related-party fee, sponsor payment or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed. facts.text: Disclosure supports monitoring but not yet a full governance read. The statements are audited by the same firm since 2003 with an opinion on internal control, the auditor named the valuation of patient receivables, including denied claims, as a critical audit matter, and the quarterly reports and slides reconcile the adjusted measures. Covenant compliance is stated without the ratios achieved, and directors' independence, compensation and beneficial ownership are in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the Medium rating reflects the limits of the evidence as well as the behaviour observed. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against reading Medium as benign is that shareholder returns have begun to exceed the cash left after growth spending and partner distributions, in the same year lender restrictions were loosened and the repurchase authorization was raised to USD 1.0 billion. If the executed documents show wide restricted-payment capacity, that pattern would be a deliberate policy of leaning on the revolver and bond market, and the view would move to higher risk, although the arithmetic is thin, because the shortfall of USD 62.9 million compares with operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million. The view would move to Low if the proxy statement shows independent oversight and dispersed ownership, returns fall back below free cash flow and leverage keeps falling. A partner asking the company to buy its interest, or claim review delaying collections beyond the bad-debt reserve already taken, would also change the view because either reaches cash flow without any change in policy. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 44; calculation C11; calculation C10

facts.text: In May 2026 the company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034 at par, raising about USD 491 million net, and used the proceeds with cash to redeem USD 400 million of the USD 800 million 2028 notes at par and repay USD 100 million of the revolver, recording a USD 3.2 million loss on early extinguishment. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Payment policy and claim review, not demand, are the dominant credit risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 lifts Medicare rates by only 2.3% from 2026-10-01, below the 3.5% to 4.0% rise the company guides for salaries and benefits per employee, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on its largest payer. Claim review compounds this: coverage rises from about 11.9% of Medicare claims to about 63% on 2027-01-01, 5.29x as many, and in Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the validation rate needed to opt out of full pre-claim review in the second or third cycle. Bad-debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 revenue against 1.9% a year earlier, and receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in nine months against USD 18.8 million. Delay and denial therefore reach cash flow before they reach reported demand. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings growth, not debt repayment, is what lowers leverage, and the pace is set to slow. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 to USD 346.6 million, and the nine-month margin was 21.77% against 21.23% because the extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58%. Total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.96x at 2025-12-31 and 1.88x at 2026-09-30, since last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 8.76% above FY2025 while debt is 4.35% higher. Guidance of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million for 2026 implies Q4 growth of only 4.77% to 10.73%, so further deleveraging needs earnings growth or repayment that management has not committed to. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

facts.text: The strongest evidence against a sound reading is the pairing of rising shareholder returns with wider claim review. facts.label: Company description and operating model

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: New entry is limited by capital and regulation but the limit is eroding at the edges. Certificate-of-need laws cover about 36% of licensed beds, yet North Carolina repealed its requirement for certain providers in July 2026 and the company accelerated the amortization of its asset there by USD 2.9 million. Entry still needs hospital-scale capital and Medicare qualification, including the rule that a set share of admissions must come from listed medical conditions, so it is slow, but where approval is no longer needed a rival's new beds would compete for the company's referral sources directly. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario that fits this issuer is payment friction meeting pay growth. From 2027-01-01 about 63% of Medicare claims, up from about 11.9%, go through pre-claim or post-payment review, while the Medicare rate rises 2.3% and pay per employee 3.5% to 4.0%. In Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the opt-out validation rate in the second or third cycle, so full pre-claim review stayed in force there. The first break is in collections: review lengthens the time to payment and lifts denials, bad-debt reserves stay at the 2.7% of revenue seen in Q3 instead of easing to the guided 2.0% to 2.5%, and the receivables build of USD 89.5 million in nine months repeats. Growth capital spending is guided at USD 695 million to USD 755 million, repurchases were USD 203.7 million in nine months and dividends are about USD 79 million for 2026, so liquidity distress is avoided if growth and repurchases are slowed when collections weaken. The scenario fails only if repurchases and the committed projects of about USD 535 million continue while collections are delayed and the revolver funds the gap, which would raise secured debt ahead of the notes and shorten the runway to the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities. We do not assume default: the evidence shows enough resilience to avoid distress with an ordinary management response, but covenant headroom is not established, so the point at which the tests bind is unknown.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 17, 43; calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C16

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Encompass Health presents an adequate business profile supported by owned scale in a rule-priced, non-discretionary service and an earnings base that is growing, but credit quality is constrained by payer concentration under widening claim review, capital allocation that has outrun cash flow and pay growth above the Medicare update. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because issuer-defined free cash flow converts 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA before growth capital, although taxes and growth spending are lowering the share. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for the 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities, which are 68.51% of face value, backed by liquidity of USD 947.6 million and a revolver to 2031. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer or rating data were supplied. The primary downside path is slower Medicare collection under wider review combined with pay growth above the rate update while repurchases continue. Further analysis would require the covenant ratios achieved, the executed credit agreement and indentures, claim-review outcome data, ratings, peer data and the proxy statement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 31, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C16

## Findings
### Bottom line

Encompass Health's leverage is low and still falling, but only because earnings are growing: debt has not fallen and 2026 shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow after joint-venture distributions, so creditor protection rests on management's capital allocation.

At 2026-09-30 total debt was USD 2,599.1 million: 1.67x trailing reported EBITDA and 1.88x the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, which deducts joint-venture partners' income. Liquidity was USD 947.6 million, and no significant debt falls due before 2028. Interest cover is 10.55x on cash interest paid for FY2025, but cash interest for the last twelve months and the covenant ratios achieved are not printed, so cover at the latest date and covenant headroom are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17, 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 163, 166; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17
### Key findings

Leverage fell on earnings growth, not repayment. Total debt was USD 2,497.8 million at 2024-12-31, USD 2,490.8 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 2,599.1 million at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,186.6 million in FY2024 to USD 1,404.1 million in FY2025 and USD 1,552.6 million over the last twelve months. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore moved from 2.11x to 1.77x to 1.67x, and net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.03x to 1.72x to 1.62x. Debt rose by USD 108.3 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, the period in which the company replaced its revolving facility, used new 2034 notes to redeem half of the 2028 notes and sold a further USD 100.0 million of the 2034 notes in August 2026 to repay part of the revolver.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17, 18, 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 163, 198; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C12; calculation C15; calculation C31; calculation C21

The issuer's own earnings measure is the more conservative guide to cash that reaches the parent. The issuer states only an Adjusted EBITDA, which deducts the income of noncontrolling interests, USD 160.9 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and adds back share-based compensation. Reported EBITDA, calculated here from pre-tax income, interest and depreciation, is USD 134.9 million higher than the issuer's measure for that period. On the issuer's measure total debt is 2.26x, 1.96x and 1.88x Adjusted EBITDA at the three dates, in line with the issuer's own rounded 2.0x at 2025-12-31 and 1.9x at 2026-09-30. Joint-venture partners received USD 141.8 million of distributions in the nine months, so the deduction is a cash cost and not an accounting convention.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 24, 47, 48; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C16; calculation C27

Cash generation is strong but is largely absorbed by growth spending and distributions. In FY2025 net cash from operating activities of USD 1,175.6 million funded USD 736.4 million of capital spending and USD 152.1 million of joint-venture distributions, leaving USD 287.1 million; dividends and repurchases took USD 229.1 million of that and left USD 58.0 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 the same sequence left USD 198.7 million before dividends of USD 57.9 million and repurchases of USD 203.7 million, a shortfall of USD 62.9 million in a period when total debt rose by USD 108.3 million. Growth capital spending was USD 451.2 million in those nine months and capital spending ran at 12.88% of net operating revenues, so the pace at which leverage keeps falling is mainly a management choice.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 165, 166; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14; calculation C11; calculation C30; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C31

Interest cover is comfortable but cannot be carried to the latest date on a cash basis. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 8.08x in FY2024 and 10.55x in FY2025. Cash interest paid exceeded interest expense by USD 9.9 million in FY2025, and the company also capitalised USD 17.6 million of interest, and the annual report does not reconcile the cash paid with the expense. The quarterly reports do not print cash interest paid, so cover for the last twelve months is not calculable on that basis; against income-statement interest expense it is 12.23x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 162, 166, 196; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C18; calculation C8

Liquidity is ample and refinancing risk is remote before 2028. At 2026-09-30 cash of USD 76.2 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 871.4 million, after USD 75.0 million drawn and USD 53.6 million of letters of credit, gave liquidity of USD 947.6 million, or 0.36x total debt. The revolver matures on 2031-03-09, so no facility expires within twelve months, and scheduled principal through 2027 is only USD 56.2 million. The maturity wall then builds from USD 436.0 million in 2028 to USD 850.8 million in 2030, which is 32.35% of scheduled principal, and USD 515.1 million in 2031. Restricted cash of USD 24.0 million and restricted marketable securities of USD 158.5 million, held mainly for the captive insurer and joint-venture obligations, are excluded from liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17, 18, 20, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C20; calculation C25; calculation C39

The four senior note series, which are unsecured and fixed rate, carry USD 2,169.2 million of the USD 2,599.1 million total, with the revolver at USD 75.0 million, finance leases at USD 274.9 million and other notes payable at USD 80.0 million. Only the revolver is stated to be secured, so debt through the senior notes is 1.45x reported EBITDA; the finance leases and other notes are not ranked in the filings and sit outside that stack. Operating lease liabilities of USD 204.3 million and purchase obligations of USD 197.4 million sit outside the debt figure, and no pension, derivative, factoring or consent-decree obligation was found in any source.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17, 18, 19, 24, 42, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 197, 199; calculation C40; calculation C24; calculation C23; calculation C38
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a benign reading is that growth and returns are being financed at the margin by debt. Capital spending of USD 617.2 million in nine months compares with a 2026 plan of USD 920 million to USD 995 million and about USD 535 million still to spend on projects under construction, and the board raised the repurchase authorization in July 2026. Receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in the nine months against USD 18.8 million a year earlier, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, which the issuer attributes to a billing and collecting disruption after a system conversion. If operating cash flow does not cover the remaining planned spending, or repurchases continue above free cash flow, leverage on the issuer's measure would stop falling. The view would improve if debt were repaid from free cash flow while EBITDA keeps growing, and weaken if trailing EBITDA fell, if the revolver were drawn to fund distributions, or if the covenant ratios, once supplied, showed less headroom than the compliance statements imply.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 35, 43, 44; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C42
### Limitations

EBITDA is not stated by the issuer, so reported EBITDA is calculated and every leverage and cover ratio rests on that calculation; the issuer-adjusted ratios are shown beside it. Last-twelve-month figures are constructed from the annual and nine-month statements, and the nine-month statements are unaudited. The covenant ratios achieved, their headroom, the leverage-test definition's pro forma adjustments and the 2026 revolver margin are not printed, and the executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant capacity is not established. Cash interest paid is printed only for the full years, cash taxes only for the full years and nine months 2026, and the third-quarter cash flow statement only as operating cash flow in the slides. Year-end 2024 revolver availability uses the commitment the annual report states in the present tense. The figures agree with the evidence trace in the Source readiness work and none of it is corrected.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Encompass Health is a scaled, government-paid inpatient rehabilitation operator with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so creditors face payment-policy and capital-allocation risk rather than ownership-extraction risk, though governance visibility is only moderate on the filings supplied.

Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and 92% of patients are referred from acute-care hospitals, so a payment-rule or referral shock would reach revenue directly. Growth depends on opening new capacity, and shareholder returns of USD 261.6 million in those nine months exceeded the cash left after capital spending and joint-venture distributions. We rate sponsor and governance risk Medium because disclosed behaviour is mixed and the proxy statement and executed debt documents are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 33, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 165; calculation C1; calculation C10; calculation C11
### Key findings

Payment policy, not demand, is the main business risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, with Medicare alone at 65.7% for the nine months and 66.3% in the third quarter. Rates are reset each year by the federal payer, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 adds a net 2.3% to Medicare payment rates from October 2026, which supports pricing. The same payer is widening claim review: a demonstration that puts claims through pre-claim or post-payment review reached Texas in March 2026 and California in May 2026, and from January 2027 will cover about 63% of the company's Medicare claims. Denied claims of USD 39.0 million were under review at 2025-12-31, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, so slower or lower collection is where a payment-policy shock would first reach cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124, 161; calculation C1

Referral and partner relationships concentrate operating risk in counterparties the filings do not quantify. About 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures with health systems that also refer patients. Partners hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million, can require the company to buy certain interests at fair value, and received USD 141.8 million of distributions in the nine months to 2026-09-30. The company lists partner operating or financial strain as a risk, so a partner problem would be both a volume risk and a possible cash call.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12, 19; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C2

Growth is capital-hungry, so cash flow is committed to expansion before it is available for debt reduction. The network added 16 hospitals between the end of 2023 and 2026-09-30, and new capacity contributed 2.9 percentage points of the 5.2% discharge growth in the nine months, which is more than half of it. The 2026 capital plan is USD 920 million to USD 995 million, of which USD 225 million to USD 240 million is maintenance, with about USD 535 million more to finish projects now under construction. The non-maintenance part is discretionary, which gives management a lever in a downturn, but it also means leverage falls only if growth spending slows or earnings keep outrunning it.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 36, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11; calculation C9; calculation C7; calculation C17

No sponsor, fund or controlling holder is identified, so sponsor-exit and fee-extraction risks are absent from the record, but the concentration of ownership is not established. The shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, non-affiliate market value was about USD 12.2 billion at 2025-06-30, the board chair is a director separate from the chief executive, related-party transactions were not material in 2025, 2024 or 2023, and the share count fell 1.30% between 2026-02-12 and 2026-10-22. The beneficial-ownership table sits in the 2026 proxy statement, which was not supplied, so a large holder with influence over distributions cannot be excluded.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3, 132, 151, 157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C13

Shareholder returns are the creditor-relevant behaviour to watch, and they are rising while evidence of the legal room for them is not supplied. The quarterly dividend rose from USD 0.17 to USD 0.19 per share in July 2025 and to USD 0.21 in July 2026, repurchases rose from USD 31.1 million in FY2024 to USD 158.0 million in FY2025 and USD 203.7 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the board raised the repurchase authorization to USD 1.0 billion in July 2026. Dividends and repurchases took 19.49% of operating cash flow in FY2025 and 27.32% in the nine months, and in the nine months they exceeded the USD 198.7 million left after capital spending and joint-venture distributions by USD 62.9 million. The March 2026 credit agreement also relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, which widens the room for such returns, while no related-party fee, sponsor payment or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 136, 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 43, 44; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

Disclosure supports monitoring but not yet a full governance read. The statements are audited by the same firm since 2003 with an opinion on internal control, the auditor named the valuation of patient receivables, including denied claims, as a critical audit matter, and the quarterly reports and slides reconcile the adjusted measures. Covenant compliance is stated without the ratios achieved, and directors' independence, compensation and beneficial ownership are in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the Medium rating reflects the limits of the evidence as well as the behaviour observed.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against reading Medium as benign is that shareholder returns have begun to exceed the cash left after growth spending and partner distributions, in the same year lender restrictions were loosened and the repurchase authorization was raised to USD 1.0 billion. If the executed documents show wide restricted-payment capacity, that pattern would be a deliberate policy of leaning on the revolver and bond market, and the view would move to higher risk, although the arithmetic is thin, because the shortfall of USD 62.9 million compares with operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million. The view would move to Low if the proxy statement shows independent oversight and dispersed ownership, returns fall back below free cash flow and leverage keeps falling. A partner asking the company to buy its interest, or claim review delaying collections beyond the bad-debt reserve already taken, would also change the view because either reaches cash flow without any change in policy.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 44; calculation C11; calculation C10
### Limitations

- Board independence, committee structure, compensation design and beneficial ownership are not established because the 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so the Medium governance rating could move either way once it is read.

- The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens rests on the company's own summaries, which limits how firmly distributions can be called a policy choice rather than a constraint.

- Geographic concentration in Florida and Texas is measured by hospital and bed counts, not revenue, so the concentration finding could be understated if those hospitals earn more than the average hospital.
- The effect of expanded claim review on collections cannot be quantified from the filings, so the payment-policy risk is stated as a direction and is not sized.
- Growth targets, opening dates and guidance are management statements and tentative, so the conclusion that growth is funded from cash flow and the revolver describes a plan, not an outcome.
- Partner put-right terms and timing are disclosed only as a fair-value formula, so the size and timing of any cash call from a partner exit is not established.

No sponsor transaction, buyout, merger or acquisition is described in the sources, and none is pending; the 2026 activity is refinancing and a small disposal. On March 9, 2026 the company entered a new credit agreement with Truist Bank as agent that replaced the 2022 agreement, moved the revolver maturity to March 2031, lowered the fee on undrawn commitments by 5 bp, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, and raised the swingline sublimit from USD 25 million to USD 40 million. It drew USD 250.0 million on the revolver that month to retire the old facility.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ehc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.2_2026-04-30_ehcq12026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5

In August 2026 it sold a further USD 100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% of principal, raising about USD 97 million net, to repay part of the revolver. The 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced, so the refinancing extended maturities at a higher running cost.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ehc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.2_2026-08-05_ehcq22026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C15; calculation C16

### Overall governance view

Overall, Encompass Health presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is rising shareholder returns, with repurchases of USD 203.7 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and shareholder returns that exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million, which matters because it competes with debt reduction while the lender restrictions were loosened in March 2026, and implies a policy-driven rather than structural risk. Countervailing evidence is that earnings growth is lowering leverage, no sponsor, related-party leakage or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed, and the maturity profile was extended. Further analysis requires the 2026 proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indentures, and the covenant ratios achieved.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Encompass Health is a sound credit with low leverage whose main threat is Medicare payment policy and claim review, so creditors are protected today but depend on management keeping growth spending and repurchases within cash flow.

Total debt of USD 2,599.1 million at 2026-09-30 was 1.88x the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, liquidity was USD 947.6 million and no significant debt matures before 2028. Medicare and Medicare Advantage paid 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and claim review will reach about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, up from about 11.9%. In the nine months, shareholder returns exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million while total debt rose USD 108.3 million, and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains. No rating is assigned, and covenant headroom is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 31, 33, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C27
### Key findings

Payment policy and claim review, not demand, are the dominant credit risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 lifts Medicare rates by only 2.3% from 2026-10-01, below the 3.5% to 4.0% rise the company guides for salaries and benefits per employee, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on its largest payer. Claim review compounds this: coverage rises from about 11.9% of Medicare claims to about 63% on 2027-01-01, 5.29x as many, and in Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the validation rate needed to opt out of full pre-claim review in the second or third cycle. Bad-debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 revenue against 1.9% a year earlier, and receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in nine months against USD 18.8 million. Delay and denial therefore reach cash flow before they reach reported demand.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30, 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C4; calculation C11; calculation C27

Earnings growth, not debt repayment, is what lowers leverage, and the pace is set to slow. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 to USD 346.6 million, and the nine-month margin was 21.77% against 21.23% because the extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58%. Total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.96x at 2025-12-31 and 1.88x at 2026-09-30, since last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 8.76% above FY2025 while debt is 4.35% higher. Guidance of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million for 2026 implies Q4 growth of only 4.77% to 10.73%, so further deleveraging needs earnings growth or repayment that management has not committed to.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

Liquidity and maturity timing give creditors a long runway, but the bond wall is concentrated. Liquidity was USD 947.6 million at 2026-09-30, and the undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million, which runs to 2031-03-09, covers the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value, and the 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced. Net debt was USD 2,522.9 million, or USD 2,543.8 million pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-15 at its declared amount of USD 20.9 million, which is 1.62x reported EBITDA or 1.64x pro forma.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 18, 20, 40; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C16

Capital allocation is the controllable risk and it is moving the wrong way. Operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capital spending of USD 617.2 million and partner distributions of USD 141.8 million left USD 198.7 million, against dividends and repurchases of USD 261.6 million. On the issuer's own measure, which starts from Adjusted EBITDA and deducts cash interest, cash taxes and maintenance capital spending, the nine months left USD 634.2 million, and after growth capital of USD 451.2 million and shareholder returns the result was a shortfall of USD 78.6 million against a surplus of USD 82.1 million a year earlier. The two measures differ in perimeter but agree in direction. About USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remained at 2026-09-30, 4.69x the nine-month repurchases of USD 203.7 million, and management gives no debt-reduction assumption for 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C25

Cash conversion is good but slipping as taxes and growth capital rise. Issuer-defined free cash flow was 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA in nine months against 62.48% a year earlier and 64.51% in FY2025, and the 2026 guidance of USD 770 million to USD 865 million implies 55.20% to 61.13% of guided Adjusted EBITDA. Cash tax payments were USD 87.3 million higher than in the nine months of 2025, equal to 78.58% of the USD 111.1 million gain in Adjusted EBITDA and partly tax paid in 2026 for an underpayment in 2025, and maintenance capital spending rose USD 25.5 million. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending, which management can slow, but about USD 535 million is still to be spent on projects already under construction.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C18

Interest cover is comfortable on every basis available. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 10.55x in FY2025 and income-statement interest 12.23x over the last twelve months. On guided cash interest of USD 115 million to USD 125 million and guided Adjusted EBITDA, cover would be 11.16x to 12.30x, although the issuer's cash interest measure ran USD 19.5 million below the cash paid in the annual report for 2025, so the cash-basis ratio could be lower.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17

Referral and partner dependence concentrate operating risk that the filings do not size. About 92% of patients come from acute-care hospitals, which also run competing rehabilitation units, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures whose partners received USD 141.8 million in nine months, 14.81% of operating cash flow, and hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million. A partner's distress or exit would hit volume and could call cash, in an amount that is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

The sector structure supports pricing, but its protective barriers are thinning at the edges. The industry outside the company is highly fragmented, patients aged 75 and over are expected to grow about 4% a year through 2030, and about 36% of licensed beds sit in states with certificate-of-need laws, but North Carolina repealed its certificate-of-need requirement for certain providers in July 2026. The annual Medicare update fell from 2.6% for fiscal 2026 to 2.3% for fiscal 2027, and a reform that paid all post-acute care under one system would, on an advisory-body estimate the company cannot verify, cut inpatient rehabilitation payments by 15%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 29, 34, 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 37; calculation C22

Covenant and legal protection cannot be established, so none is relied on here. The credit agreement sets a maximum leverage ratio of 4.50x and a minimum interest coverage of 3.0x and the company states compliance, but the ratios achieved, the adjustments in their definitions and the executed agreements are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a sound reading is the pairing of rising shareholder returns with wider claim review. Returns have begun to exceed cash after growth spending, total debt rose USD 108.3 million in nine months, lender limits on restricted payments were relaxed in March 2026 and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains; at the same time review reaches about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, no Alabama hospital reached the opt-out rate in the second or third review cycle, and a Q3 bad-debt reserve of 2.7% of revenue shows how quickly collection can slip. The strongest evidence in favour is the company's own room to respond: growth capital spending guided at USD 695 million to USD 755 million is 6.26x to 6.80x the USD 111.1 million fall in Adjusted EBITDA that would take it back to its FY2025 level, where total debt would be 2.05x Adjusted EBITDA, and management guides Q4 bad-debt reserves back to 2.0% to 2.5% of revenue.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 31, 35, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C25

The view would weaken if the bad-debt reserve stayed above 2.7% of revenue after the effect of the Q2 system conversion fades, if the revolver were drawn to fund repurchases, or if total debt over Adjusted EBITDA rose above its FY2024 level of 2.26x. It would improve if debt were repaid from free cash flow while earnings keep growing, or if the executed credit agreement and indentures showed wide room under the leverage and restricted-payment tests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C1
### Limitations

- No rating, market price or peer was supplied, so the comparison of this business with typical leveraged-credit issuers and any relative-value view are not established, and the sound-credit conclusion rests on the issuer's own history and filings.

- Review outcomes are given only in words for the Alabama hospitals, with no validation rates, denial amounts or payment timing, so the sensitivity to a payment delay of 10 days is an illustration and not a forecast, and the claim-review risk to cash flow could be larger or smaller than shown.
- No independent forecast was run, so the conclusion that earnings keep growing and leverage keeps falling reads management's 2026 guidance and not a tested projection.

- The earnings-fall scenario is anchored to the FY2025 level of Adjusted EBITDA and not to any covenant test, so it says nothing about how far earnings could fall before a covenant test bound, and no covenant headroom is stated.

- The issuer's guided cash interest is USD 19.5 million below the cash interest paid reported for 2025 for reasons the filings do not give, so the cash-basis interest-cover conclusion could be somewhat lower than the ratios shown.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is earnings growth that lowers leverage without repayment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 and total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.88x at 2026-09-30, because extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58% against an average margin of 21.23%; this widens the gap between cash flow and debt service and supports a low probability of distress while volumes keep growing.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

The second strength is a long liquidity and maturity runway. Liquidity of USD 947.6 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million to 2031 cover the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x, so refinancing risk is remote until 2028 and any slower earnings would be absorbed before creditors are affected.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 40; calculation C2; calculation C16

The third strength is non-discretionary, rule-priced demand that is still growing. Discharges rose 5.7% in Q3 and the Medicare rate update of 2.3% from 2026-10-01 sets price in advance, with an ageing population adding about 4% a year to the 75-and-over group, which gives revenue visibility that supports debt service through a normal cycle.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14

The fourth strength is discretionary growth spending. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending and the 2026 growth plan of USD 695 million to USD 755 million is more than six times the USD 111.1 million fall in earnings used in the downside, so management can protect liquidity in a downturn by slowing expansion.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

The fifth strength is owned real estate against an unsecured bond structure. The company owns the building at 79.19% of its hospitals and only the revolver is stated to be secured, so a large asset base sits outside the secured claim, although its value and the recovery it would support are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The first weakness is payer concentration under widening review. Medicare and Medicare Advantage paid 81.8% of revenue and review will cover about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, up from about 11.9%, so a delay or denial pushes cash collection back before any change in demand, a mechanism already visible in a bad-debt reserve of 2.7% of Q3 revenue and in Alabama, where no hospital reached the opt-out rate in two cycles.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; calculation C4; calculation C15; calculation C27

The second weakness is capital allocation that outruns cash flow. Shareholder returns exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million while debt rose USD 108.3 million, and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains, so leverage can stop falling by choice and debt holders carry that policy risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C25

The third weakness is labour cost that is outrunning the Medicare price. Salaries and benefits are 51.72% of revenue and guided to rise 3.5% to 4.0% per employee against a 2.3% Medicare update, so margins depend on staffing productivity that has to keep improving to hold the 21.77% nine-month margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 30; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C20

The fourth weakness is a concentrated bond wall at a higher cost. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value and new 2034 debt carries a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes, so refinancing depends on market access in those years and will probably cost more interest.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; calculation C2; calculation C16

The fifth weakness is dependence on referral sources and joint-venture partners. About 92% of patients are referred by acute-care hospitals that also run competing units, and partners took USD 141.8 million of distributions in nine months while holding put rights on terms that are not disclosed, so volume and cash calls can change without any change in policy.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

### Company description and operating model

Encompass Health owns and operates inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico, 67 of them joint ventures with health systems, and reports one segment, so the credit rests on a single service line paid mostly by one federal payer. Revenue of USD 6,338.1 million over the last twelve months is inpatient discharges multiplied by a net price per discharge: in the nine months discharges rose 5.20% and price 3.89%, and new hospitals supplied 2.9 percentage points of the 5.2% discharge growth, so about half of volume growth needs capital before it earns. The model supports cash-flow visibility because payment is set by rule in advance and the conditions treated are not deferred, but it weakens liquidity preservation whenever growth capital is committed ahead of earnings.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 34, 36; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21

Cyclicality is low and concentration is high. Medicare and Medicare Advantage together paid 81.8% of nine-month revenue, 92% of patients arrive from acute-care hospitals and Florida and Texas hold 31.21% of hospitals, so a payment rule, a referral change or a regional disruption each reaches a large share of cash flow at once. Cash generation is real, with operating cash flow of USD 1,303.7 million over the last twelve months, but 73.10% of nine-month capital spending is growth, so the cash left for debt reduction depends on management's choices more than on the business.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C21
### Ownership and group structure

Encompass Health is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so sponsor-extraction risks are absent, but the beneficial-ownership table sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied and concentration of holdings is not established. Subsidiary guarantors guarantee the credit agreement, which is secured by personal property, and give full and unconditional senior unsecured guarantees of the notes, while non-guarantor subsidiaries are not summarised separately, so the claims that rank ahead of the notes at those subsidiaries cannot be measured. Joint-venture partners hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million, and their share of income equals 13.66% of nine-month reported EBITDA, so that part of group earnings does not reach the parent.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 8, 18, 44, 45; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19; calculation C21

Financial policy is the creditor-relevant behaviour. The company reports leverage on its own Adjusted EBITDA and no leverage target appears in the sources. The quarterly dividend rose to USD 0.21 per share in July 2026, repurchases reached USD 203.7 million in nine months and the board raised the authorization to USD 1.0 billion, with about USD 955 million remaining. Growth comes from new hospitals and no acquisition is described or pending, so event risk from large deals is low, but shareholder returns now exceed the cash left after growth, which is why sponsor and governance risk is rated Medium and why creditor alignment is partial.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 43, 44; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C25
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Volume is the stronger driver and price is set mostly by rule. Discharges rose 5.7% in Q3, 3.0% same-store and 2.7% from new hospitals, and Q3 occupancy of 77.0% leaves room to fill existing beds, which is cheaper growth than building. The Medicare update is 2.3% from 2026-10-01 after 2.6% a year earlier, managed care pricing is guided at 3.5% to 4.0% and Medicaid is only 3.0% of revenue, so pricing power is weakest with the largest payer and better only where contracts are negotiated.

Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7, 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 33, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C22

Revenue is predictable, regulated and concentrated, not cyclical or structurally declining, because rehabilitation admissions follow stroke, brain injury and hip fracture that are not deferred. It is exposed to substitution at the margin, since nursing homes may market rehabilitation to patients who do not need intensive therapy, and to reform of post-acute payment. Medicare fee-for-service rose to 66.3% of Q3 revenue from 64.1% while Medicare Advantage fell to 15.7% from 16.6%, and claim review applies only to fee-for-service claims, so the mix shift raises exposure at the moment the review widens.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10, 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 65; calculation C4
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Labour is the main cost and it flexes partly with occupied beds. Salaries and benefits were 52.2% of Q3 revenue against 53.1% a year earlier, employees per occupied bed were 3.38 against 3.42 and contract labour fell 23.2%, which is how margin was held while pay per employee rose. Because Medicare pays a fixed amount per discharge and the hospital keeps the difference from its cost, every saving or overrun is a margin change, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.53% in Q3 against 20.31%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C5; calculation C20

Margin is easier to defend against slower volume than against wage inflation. The incremental margin of 27.58% shows operating leverage that cuts both ways, so slower volume would reduce earnings faster than revenue. Pay per employee is guided up 3.5% to 4.0% against a 2.3% Medicare update, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on 65.7% of revenue, and pre-opening and ramp-up costs of USD 15.8 million in nine months, guided at USD 20 million to USD 24 million for the year, weigh on margin while new hospitals fill. Downside cost flexibility sits mostly in staffing and hiring, because occupancy costs are only 0.9% of Q3 revenue on largely owned buildings and depreciation is already 5.9%.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 34; calculation C5; calculation C11
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is high and mostly chosen. Capital spending was 12.88% of nine-month revenue, of which USD 166.0 million, 26.90%, was maintenance and USD 451.2 million, 73.10%, was growth; the 2026 plan is USD 920 million to USD 995 million with USD 225 million to USD 240 million of maintenance, and about USD 535 million more is needed to finish projects under construction. On the issuer's measure 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA converts to free cash flow before growth capital and shareholder returns, so cash for debt reduction is what remains after management decides how much growth to fund.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C10

Other claims on cash sit beside the debt figure. Finance leases of USD 274.9 million are inside it, while operating lease liabilities of USD 204.3 million, purchase obligations of USD 197.4 million and future interest of USD 544.5 million on debt other than finance leases are outside it. Cash interest is guided at USD 115 million to USD 125 million and cash taxes at USD 200 million to USD 220 million for 2026, so fixed charges are covered many times by Adjusted EBITDA, and the ability to slow growth spending is the main protection if earnings fall before the 2028 to 2031 maturities.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17; calculation C26
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is local and moderate. The industry outside the company is fragmented and the main competitors are rehabilitation units inside acute-care hospitals, which can be formidable where a large system dominates the local market, and one public company that mainly provides other post-acute care also runs 38 rehabilitation hospitals. Because 92% of patients are referred by acute-care hospitals, a system that opens its own unit can divert referrals, a volume risk market by market and not a pricing risk, since Medicare sets the price.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 14

New entry is limited by capital and regulation but the limit is eroding at the edges. Certificate-of-need laws cover about 36% of licensed beds, yet North Carolina repealed its requirement for certain providers in July 2026 and the company accelerated the amortization of its asset there by USD 2.9 million. Entry still needs hospital-scale capital and Medicare qualification, including the rule that a set share of admissions must come from listed medical conditions, so it is slow, but where approval is no longer needed a rival's new beds would compete for the company's referral sources directly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C22

Substitutes pull at the margin. Nursing homes may market rehabilitation to patients who do not need intensive therapy, and a bundled-payment programme that covers 2% of the company's discharges, with 89 of its hospitals in the affected markets, gives acute-care hospitals a financial reason to choose the cheapest setting, although they may not restrict a patient's choice. The effect is on lower-acuity volume and is small today, and it would matter to creditors only if bundled payment widened.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14

Buyer power is high in structure and low in practice. Medicare pays 65.7% of revenue and sets price by rule, while Medicare Advantage at 16.1% and managed care at 10.7% are negotiated under contracts that typically run one to three years, with typical rate increases of 2% to 4% in 2025, and acute-care referral sources are the gatekeepers. The company cannot negotiate with its largest payer, so rate rules and review programmes pass straight into margin and cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 30; calculation C22

Supplier power sits mainly in clinical labour. Salaries and benefits are 51.72% of revenue and guided to rise 3.5% to 4.0% per employee, whereas supplies were 4.0% of Q3 revenue against 4.4%, so wage competition rather than input cost is what can compress margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C20
### Policy and macro factors

Only three categories change the credit view. Regulatory policy is the largest, because the annual payment rule, the review demonstration and any move to a single post-acute payment system act directly on price and cash collection. Social change supports demand, since the population aged 75 and over is expected to grow about 4% a year through 2030 and the average Medicare patient is about 77. Technology mattered in 2026: a billing and collecting disruption after a system conversion pushed bad-debt reserves to 2.7% of Q3 revenue from 1.9%, a direct cash effect of an operating change, which management expects to ease to 2.0% to 2.5% in Q4.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7

Economic factors and currency are not a primary driver of credit quality. The company operates in the United States and Puerto Rico, wage inflation is dealt with under cost, and the only reference to tariffs is a general risk statement with no stated effect.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Credit-translated SWOT

The credit-supportive factors are earnings growth that is lowering leverage, liquidity of USD 947.6 million with a revolver to 2031 that covers the 2028 maturities 2.00x, rule-priced non-discretionary demand and growth capital that management can slow. The credit constraints are payer concentration under widening review, capital allocation that has outrun cash flow, pay growth above the Medicare update and a bond wall of 68.51% of face value in 2028, 2030 and 2031.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C2; calculation C16

Only some opportunities could improve credit quality. Q3 occupancy of 77.0% leaves room to fill existing beds; planned additions of 4.66% to 5.05% of licensed beds in 2026 add capacity; revenue growth has so far carried an incremental margin above the average; and repayment of the revolver from free cash flow would raise protection further. The threats are review extended beyond the announced hospitals, a move to one post-acute payment system that an advisory body estimated would cut payments by 15%, and loss of a joint-venture partner or referral relationship.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C5; calculation C23

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months management guides 2026 revenue of USD 6,450 million to USD 6,500 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million, raised from USD 1,365 million to USD 1,395 million, with eight new hospitals and further bed additions in 2026 and a similar programme planned for 2027. The tailwinds are the 2.3% Medicare update from 2026-10-01 and managed care pricing of 3.5% to 4.0%, which support revenue and margin. The headwinds are claim review from 2027-01-01, pay growth of 3.5% to 4.0% per employee and a bad-debt reserve guided at 2.0% to 2.5% of Q4 revenue, which press on margin and cash flow. Guided free cash flow of USD 770 million to USD 865 million and a growth plan of USD 695 million to USD 755 million leave leverage falling only if earnings grow, because debt reduction and repurchases are both unset.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 31; calculation C7; calculation C8

Over three to five years management targets 6 to 10 new hospitals a year and discharge growth of 6% to 8% through 2027, and the population aged 75 and over is expected to grow about 4% a year to 2030, a tailwind to volume that supports deleveraging if capital spending is paced. The bundled-payment programme runs to December 2030 and a single post-acute payment system, if adopted, would on an advisory-body estimate cut payments by 15%, both headwinds to price. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities fall in this window, so market access at that time, not performance now, sets refinancing cost.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 46; calculation C16; calculation C22
### Downside scenario

The scenario that fits this issuer is payment friction meeting pay growth. From 2027-01-01 about 63% of Medicare claims, up from about 11.9%, go through pre-claim or post-payment review, while the Medicare rate rises 2.3% and pay per employee 3.5% to 4.0%. In Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the opt-out validation rate in the second or third cycle, so full pre-claim review stayed in force there. The first break is in collections: review lengthens the time to payment and lifts denials, bad-debt reserves stay at the 2.7% of revenue seen in Q3 instead of easing to the guided 2.0% to 2.5%, and the receivables build of USD 89.5 million in nine months repeats.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 31, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11; calculation C27

Revenue is delayed before it is lost, so cash falls before earnings. Holding the reserve 80 bp above its year-earlier level costs USD 12.88 million a quarter, 3.71% of Q3 Adjusted EBITDA, and each 10 days of added delay on the Medicare revenue under review ties up about USD 67.0 million. A delay of 30 days, with Adjusted EBITDA also falling back by USD 111.1 million to its FY2025 level, would absorb USD 312.1 million, which is 32.94% of liquidity of USD 947.6 million, and total debt would be 2.05x Adjusted EBITDA against 1.88x. The length of delay is an assumption for illustration, because the filings print no payment timing for reviewed claims.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 35; calculation C1; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C15

Management has levers well above that size. Growth capital spending is guided at USD 695 million to USD 755 million, repurchases were USD 203.7 million in nine months and dividends are about USD 79 million for 2026, so liquidity distress is avoided if growth and repurchases are slowed when collections weaken. The scenario fails only if repurchases and the committed projects of about USD 535 million continue while collections are delayed and the revolver funds the gap, which would raise secured debt ahead of the notes and shorten the runway to the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities. We do not assume default: the evidence shows enough resilience to avoid distress with an ordinary management response, but covenant headroom is not established, so the point at which the tests bind is unknown.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 17, 43; calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C16
### Overall credit view

Overall, Encompass Health presents an adequate business profile supported by owned scale in a rule-priced, non-discretionary service and an earnings base that is growing, but credit quality is constrained by payer concentration under widening claim review, capital allocation that has outrun cash flow and pay growth above the Medicare update. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because issuer-defined free cash flow converts 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA before growth capital, although taxes and growth spending are lowering the share. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for the 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities, which are 68.51% of face value, backed by liquidity of USD 947.6 million and a revolver to 2031. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer or rating data were supplied. The primary downside path is slower Medicare collection under wider review combined with pay growth above the rate update while repurchases continue. Further analysis would require the covenant ratios achieved, the executed credit agreement and indentures, claim-review outcome data, ratings, peer data and the proxy statement.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 31, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C16
Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: Medicare payment policy and claim review.
